reuse.why: All link rules (duplicate link, closed account, takeover) go into the existing shared linkBankSyncAccount, Fintegra linking uses it, and unlinkAccount now shares the new clearBankLink; the Fintegra download is a new copy of the Akahu function instead of a shared provider-download helper.

duplication.why: downloadFintegraTransactions is a verbatim copy of downloadAkahuTransactions (only the server key and log text differ), following the tree's existing copy-per-provider pattern; the link-side changes remove duplication (findOrCreateBank calls and the unlink update are centralised).

placement.why: Link rules sit in the shared link helper in accounts/app.ts, provider download and dispatch in accounts/sync.ts, the server path in server-config.ts and the type in types/models, matching where the tree keeps each.

scope.why: Focused on the four requests, apart from an unrelated import reorder in server/schedules/app.ts.

maintainability.why: One link helper now owns every pre-link check and the bank-row creation after them, which is easy to own; the per-provider download copies keep growing and the replaceExistingLink flag is threaded through every provider wrapper.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every provider link, including Fintegra, goes through linkBankSyncAccount; unlinkAccount uses clearBankLink.

disguised_duplication.where: downloadFintegraTransactions in accounts/sync.ts is an undisguised copy of downloadAkahuTransactions.

abstraction_drift.where: linkBankSyncAccount gains replaceExistingLink and has its bank argument split into institution/bankId (so the bank row is created after the checks); one flag-driven branch (refuse vs clear the existing link) is added; no call site bypasses it. The only provider special case (fintegra next to akahu) is in processBankSyncDownload in sync.ts, outside the helper.
